analysis.title: China: Three things in China
key_insights: The PBOC moved its policy rate benchmark on Oct 30 from the 7-day reverse repo rate (1.4%) to the overnight reverse repo rate (1.25%). GS views this as equivalent to a 5-10bp cut to front-end interbank interest rates.
GS thinks the timing of the PBOC announcement was likely related to the Huafa credit risk, related mutual fund redemptions, and continued equity market weakness.

Media reported on Nov 1 that financial regulators including the PBOC will meet major banks on Nov 2 to discuss optimizing the relending policy for stock buybacks and shareholding increases, presumably to help stabilize the equity market.
GS believes recent events show policymakers' focus on ensuring financial stability and the trend of Chinese interest rates grinding lower.
Official NBS October PMIs dropped: manufacturing from 50.1 to 49.3 and non-manufacturing from 50.2 to 49.7.

GS reads the PMI drop as consistent with within-quarter residual seasonality: readings in quarter-end months (March, June, September, December) tend to be strong, then drop in April, July, October and January. GS interprets this as evidence of downward growth pressures and front-loaded production to boost quarter-end GDP readings.
The Fifth Plenum communique (Oct 29) focused mainly on Party self-governance, self-supervision and self-reform. The 15th Five-Year Plan proposal was already approved at the Fourth Plenum last year.
With anti-corruption efforts continuing and GS's anti-corruption index remaining elevated, GS expects the transmission from policy easing rhetoric to the economy to be blunted.

The communique called to ensure fulfilment of this year's main economic and social development goals. GS reads this as suggesting the real GDP growth target of 4.5-5% will be reached when Q4 GDP data are published.
The 21st Party Congress will be held in the second half of 2027, when the top echelon of Party leadership will be reshuffled.
